'''Leopoldo Penna Franca''' (April 7, 1959 – September 19, 2012, in [[Rio de Janeiro]], [[Brazil]])<ref>{{Cite web |title=NA Digest, V. 12, # 40 |url=https://www.netlib.org/na-digest-html/12/v12n40.html |access-date=2026-02-19 |website=www.netlib.org}}</ref> was a Brazilian-American [[mathematician]]. He received his PhD in 1987 from [[Stanford University]] in engineering under [[Thomas J. R. Hughes]]. After graduation, he worked at the [[:pt:Laboratório Nacional de Computação Científica - LNCC]] in Brazil. From 1993 to 2011, he was a full professor and researcher of mathematics at the [[University of Colorado Denver]]. From 2008 to 2010, he was a visiting professor and researcher of mathematics at the [[Federal University of Rio de Janeiro - UFRJ / Coppe]] at the [[Civil Engineering Department]] in collaboration to [[Alvaro Coutinho]]. From 2011 until 2012, he worked for [[IBM]] Research Brazil. He was known for his work on stabilized [[finite element methods]]. He was a recipient of the [[United States Association for Computational Mechanics - USACM]]. Received in 1999 the  [[Gallagher Young Investigator Award]] for "outstanding accomplishments in computational mechanics, particularly in the published literature, by a researcher 40 years old or younger".<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.usacm.org/h_a_past |title=Gallagher Young Investigator Award, 1999 – Leopoldo Franca |access-date=2012-09-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121117231331/http://www.usacm.org/h_a_past |archive-date=2012-11-17 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was listed<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-10-07 |title=Clarivate Highly Cited Researchers 2025 |url=https://clarivate.com/highly-cited-researchers/ |access-date=2026-02-19 |language=en-US}}</ref> as an ISI Highly Cited Author in Engineering by the [[ISI Web of Knowledge]], Thomson Scientific Company.
